To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inhibition of glycogen synthases kinase-3 (a protein kinase) in cultured dermal papilla cells (cells that are important for hair follicle growth) increases the expression of two dermal papilla markers, alkaline phosphatases and insulin-like growth factors, and maintains hair follicles in mouse skin in organ culture.
inhibition of GSK-3 enhances the growth of human primary dermal cells, and maintains mouse hair follicles in organ culture.
the inhibition of GSK-3 enhances the hair follicle-inducibility of cultured human DP cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of BIO in the culture of human DP cells.
hair regeneration and hair follicle-induction.
the effect of GSK-3 inhibition in the regulation of the DP cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GSK-3 inhibition may be a useful approach for maintaining the expression of DP-specific markers in cultured DP cells and hair follicles in culture.
GSK-3 inhibition is useful in the maintenance of DP cells and hair follicles.
the GSK-3 inhibitors may have a potential to be applied to regenerative medicine for the hair growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BIO may be a good candidate for the treatment of hair loss and alopecia.
the Wnt signal plays an important role for hair regeneration.
GSK-3 inhibition is a promising approach to maintain hair follicle-inducibility in DP cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

BIO can maintain the expression of ALPs and IGF- 1, two important markers of dermal papilla, which are lost during the long-term culture of DP cells, and can maintain mouse hair follicles for at least 4 days without detectible regression of hair bulbs.
the inhibition of GSK-3 may be a novel strategy to enhance the expression of DP markers and maintain the hair follicles in organ culture.
GSK-3 is a potential therapeutic target for promoting hair growth.
